A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REG research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, ImageNet and COCO generation metrics, and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds runtime and peak GPU memory measurements in Table 5.

M1.justification: The REG correction in Equation (21), its inference procedure, and the EDM2 adaptation in Appendix E.2 remain unchanged. The revised description of the Jacobian assumption does not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1D and 2D synthetic tasks, ImageNet resolutions, and COCO-2017 text-to-image evaluation. The added resource measurements use existing model and resolution coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding generation comparisons retain the same vanilla, cosine, linear, and interval CFG and AutoG comparators. The new resource analysis uses the existing vanilla CFG comparator.

E3.justification: Table 5 introduces resource profiling with runtime batch sizes of 8, 4, or 2 depending on the model and batch size 1 for memory measurements. Existing generation protocols, sample counts, and samplers are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds a supplementary analysis of REG's runtime and memory costs across six model-resolution combinations. Existing synthetic approximation analyses, Pareto curves, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E.1 retains the same Monte Carlo reward-estimation procedures. Neither version provides benchmark seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new profiling results add none.

E6.justification: The synthetic results and ImageNet/COCO scores are unchanged, including v1 Tables 2–3 matched to v2 Tables 3–4. New Table 5 reports runtime ratios of 1.21–1.88× and memory ratios of 1.21–2.82× for REG relative to CFG.

T1.justification: Section 4 changes the assumption supporting the element-wise Jacobian approximation from 'diagonally dominant' to '(approximately) diagonal,' a localized mathematical qualification. The equations, theorem statements, and appendix proofs are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint scaling, guidance as an approximation without future foresight, and REG's effectiveness. No main scientific contribution is added or withdrawn.

C2.justification: v2 characterizes measured resource overhead as generally affordable and below 2×, with an SD-XL memory exception visible in Table 5. Section 3 also qualifies terminal-only scaling as a presentation simplification of earlier guidance goals. The concluding limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a public REG code statement and repository link. The new profiling study specifies a single NVIDIA A40 GPU and batch sizes; existing appendix implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Xia et al. (2024) and a discussion of concurrent work by Pavasovic et al. (2025). It also acknowledges that Ho and Salimans originally described scaling all marginals. Publication updates to existing references do not introduce additional works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose additions, adds a runtime-and-memory subsection and acknowledgements, and updates affiliation and proceedings information. The overall narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the resource table and transposes and moves v1's appendix model-summary Table 4 into the main text as Table 2. Existing figures are reused, with local layout reflow and result-table renumbering.

improvement.justification: Table 5 makes previously unquantified computational costs assessable, while the code link and localized mathematical and attribution clarifications improve transparency. These are limited gains because the central results and proofs remain unchanged. The conclusion still calls overhead 'minor' despite the reported 2.82× SD-XL memory cost.
